plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Plasmodium lifecycle and liver/blood amplification chart from Laveran (1880) and Ross (18 December 1897 British Medical Journal 2: 1786–1788) shows 10–100 mosquito-injected sporozoites multiplying ~10,000–30,000× inside a single liver cell before invading red blood cells and bursting 10¹¹–10¹² cells every 48 hours.

teach_overlay.label: PLASMODIUM AMPLIFICATION: 1 SPOROZOITE → 30,000× PER LIVER CELL → 10¹¹–10¹² RED CELLS EVERY 48 HOURS
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Plasmodium lifecycle & liver/blood amplification chart on period paper from Laveran (1880) and Ross (18 December 1897 British Medical Journal 2: 1786–1788) showing 10–100 mosquito-injected sporozoites multiplying ~10,000–30,000× inside a single liver cell before invading red blood cells and bursting 10¹¹–10¹² cells every 48 hours
teach_overlay.scale: a single malaria parasite injected by one mosquito bite multiplies up to thirty thousand times inside one human liver cell before flooding the bloodstream with hundreds of billions of parasites
